newsitem.title: UK: Rexam sees margin improvment, but sales flat.
newsitem.headline: Rexam sees margin improvment, but sales flat.

text.p: Packaging group Rexam Plc said on Wednesday trading in the first two months of its current year had seen some margin improvement over the same period last year, but sales remained flat.

The group, which is in the middle of a major rationalisation, said flat volumes in packaging were partly responsible for the fall in profits last year to 170 million stg before exceptionals from 185 million in 1995.

The group said the results were affected by customers' efforts to compensate in 1996 for unprecedented raw material cost increases during 1995 by demanding cheaper packaging, using less or lower cost raw materials.

Food and beverage packaging, industrial packaging and healthcare packaging each suffered a drop in profitability, while building and engineering, coated films and papers, printing and beauty packaging reported an improvement.

The results reflected the group's wide ranging restructuring, asset write-offs and rationalisation of management in some areas. Total costs from the shake-up amounted to 73 million stg after tax, of which 34 million was in cash. Rexam expected that the pay back from this cash would be recouped in about two years.

The group is selling off businesses and said it expected to complete the disposals by June 1998. Rexam estimated the financial impact of the sell-off programme would be a loss of 31 million stg after tax, charged in 1996.
The reorganisation included a goodwill write off of 254 million stg, which had previously been eliminated from reserves.
Chief executive Rolf Borjesson said the group had the potential to boost turnover to three billion stg by 2000, via organic growth,joint ventures or acquisitions.
He said Rexam had to take advantage of opportunities in its markets if it were to achieve this.
Chairman Jeremy Lancaster said, "With gearing at 24 percent, a five year low, and interest cover before exceptional items of 10 times, we have a balance sheet to support this development."
Rexam's shares were 10.5 pence higher at 339 pence by 0938 GMT.
